published_source_name: Boston Police Department Crime Statistics: January 1
column20: Official BPD notes that the 2024 homicide total includes one incident ruled a homicide in 2024 that occurred in prior years. The public feed is occurrence-date based and small-N; keep pending explicit policy sign-off.

published_source_name: Boston Police Department Crime Statistics: January 1
column20: The official BPD PDF reports rape and attempted rape, but the reviewed 2024 public export contains no rape-related public rows even though the official offense workbook lists many rape codes.

published_source_name: Boston Police Department Crime Statistics: January 1
column20: The official BPD summary is 'Robbery and Attempted'. The reviewed 2024 public export exposes only code 301 and no robbery-attempt codes 341-364 from the official offense workbook.

published_source_name: Boston Police Department Crime Statistics: January 1
column20: The reviewed 2024 public export exposes only code 423 while the official offense workbook lists a much broader aggravated-assault family. The 2024 public count is about 34.6 percent below the official BPD Part One total.

published_source_name: Boston Police Department Crime Statistics: January 1
column20: The reviewed 2024 public export exposes only codes 520 and 540. It does not expose the no-force, other, or attempt burglary families listed in the official offense workbook, so the current public feed is structurally incomplete for burglary.

published_source_name: Boston Police Department Crime Statistics: January 1
column20: The raw public larceny family is close to the official BPD total (-3.9 percent before geocode loss) and retains the core 611-619 larceny subtype family needed for a useful city-share overlay.

published_source_name: Boston Police Department Crime Statistics: January 1
column20: The reviewed 2024 public export retains direct theft codes and geocodes most of them. Geocoded motor-vehicle-theft rows are within 0.7 percent of the official BPD auto-theft total.
